children: Beena Parmar Bengaluru: Infosys plans to move a quarter to a third of its workforce into specialist roles and build a team of around 6,000 frontier engineers, said people who attended a recent company event where it briefed them on the plan. The Bengaluru-based company is hiring from top Indian institutes and US campuses, often competing with AI labs for the same people, the management told its partners, advisers and analysts at a three-day annual Americas confluence in Washington, DC, last week, according to the people ET spoke with.

With more than 320,000 employees on its payroll and AI disrupting the billing rates based on the number of employees deployed on a project, India's second-largest IT services provider acknowledged that the headcount-led rate model was under pressure, three analysts separately told ET. The specialist roles, such as in AI, data and the domains in which the company operates, will be supported by a new skills framework and assessments. "Infosys said it hasn't restructured, which is a noticeably different approach from what many companies are doing right now.

It says a lot about how it's thinking about talent and change management, and about where it expects to need people in future," said Dana Daher, executive research leader at HFS Research who was present at the confluence. In some deals it's taking on clients' surplus staff and redeploying them," she said.

According to a presentation by an Infosys executive, 270,000 employees are trained on AI while 80,000 are working on coding tools. In a rare appearance, chief executive officer-designate Ashiss Kumar Dash and current CEO Salil Parekh shared stage, speaking on creating value from AI, as the company with $20 billion revenue is facing challenges when the IT industry is undergoing one of its biggest technology upheavals.

The flagship regional thought leadership event's theme centred on helping enterprises "unlock AI value" and navigate the shift from AI experimentation to enterprise-wide scaling - a message which has been across all of Infosys's 2026 Confluence events: Asia Pacific, Europe, the Middle East and Africa and the Americas.

The senior management outlined the company's plans alongside other conversations around AI, its impact on pricing, and how it plans to strategies enterprise AI and build AI at scale. Infosys did not respond to a request seeking comment on the event. Besides Parekh and Dash, other speakers and panellists included Anant Adya, head of Americas delivery who also leads AI-powered cloud platform Infosys Cobalt; and Anand Swaminathan, executive vice president and global industry leader.

title: Infy Plans to Shift One-third of its Workforce into Specialist Roles
